The committed dependency map (`.gestalt/architecture/reconciled.json` and `.gestalt/architecture/app.json`) contains the `policy -> leave-type` edge, confirming the flagged import is a sanctioned dependency and the finding is a false positive.
No code change is made to line 3 of `src/modules/policy/policy.service.ts`; the file remains byte-identical and `npm run build` plus the existing test suite remain green.

constraints: The `policy -> leave-type` dependency must be expressed only through `src/modules/leave-type/index.ts` (the owning module's public entry point); no deep import into leave-type internals is permitted.

The three imported symbols (`ILeaveTypeService`, `LeaveTypeService`, `PgLeaveTypeRepository`) must remain in use: `ILeaveTypeService` as the `PolicyService` constructor parameter type, and `LeaveTypeService`/`PgLeaveTypeRepository` inside `createPolicyService()`. Removing or rewriting the import would break the composition factory.
No runtime behaviour, constructor signatures, or public interfaces may change; this is a false-positive resolution, not a refactor.
outOfScope: Any code change to `src/modules/policy/policy.service.ts` line 3 or elsewhere — the finding is a false positive and no edit is required.
Moving the `leave-type` dependency out of `policy` or into the shared layer — the reconciled architecture intentionally owns the `policy -> leave-type` edge.
Rewiring `balance`/`leave` composition factories (Phases 2–3 of the parent feature) — those are separate phases.

entityInvariants.invariant: Must continue to construct `PolicyService` with `PgLeavePolicyRepository` and `LeaveTypeService(PgLeaveTypeRepository)`; it owns the `policy -> leave-type` composition and must not be altered.

The import must resolve to the owning module's public entry point, which re-exports `ILeaveTypeService`, `LeaveTypeService`, and `PgLeaveTypeRepository`.
